findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the status target-environment option against epic 2f79's four-flag decision: either confirm the epic's flag census is not an exhaustive per-verb cap (documenting that status may add a read-only env selector), or fold the selector into the epic's sanctioned surface so the leaf stays a clean subset.
evidence: Leaf: 'Status accepts an explicit target environment option.'
Epic 2f79: 'Ten candidates reduced to four operational flags (--max-changes, --only, --except, --max-age).'

Epic AC1 lists `status` as a canonical verb but does not enumerate a per-verb option cap, and the four-flag reduction concerned the mutate/preview candidate set; a read-only status env selector is a plausible elaboration rather than a contradicted clause -- hence cosmetic.
findings.finding: The leaf adds a status-scoped 'explicit target environment option' that is not among the parent epic's enumerated four surviving operational flags (--max-changes, --only, --except, --max-age); the epic's flag census does not mention an environment-target flag.
findings.location: Leaf 'Environment identity' / 'Status snapshot and exact contract' vs epic 2f79 decision 'Ten candidates reduced to four operational flags'
scenarios: Reviewer cross-checks the epic's four-flag decision against the leaf's status options and finds an unlisted target-environment flag.

findings.finding: The `local:<repo-env-id>` identity derivation from the checkout `.env-id` has no stated behavior when `.env-id` is absent or unreadable.
findings.suggested_fix: State that a missing/unreadable .env-id yields a hard error (or a documented sentinel like local:unknown) and must never fall back to reconciler.

findings.finding: The verdict set (HEALTHY, PAUSED, RUNNING, STALE, FOREIGN, NEVER_RUN, FAILED, CRASHED) can co-occur in one snapshot, but only PAUSED-over-STALE precedence is stated; the full precedence order is under-specified.
findings.location: Status snapshot and exact contract — verdict/exit list
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit precedence ladder to the contract section, e.g.: PAUSED > RUNNING > FOREIGN > FAILED > STALE > HEALTHY, with NEVER_RUN only when neither a record nor a live lock exists, and give the resulting exit code for each dominant case.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how the canary bounds the observed inter-snapshot lease against its fixed job timeout-minutes (e.g. cap the wait, fail loudly, or assert lease << runner budget) so a large configured lock_lease_secs cannot silently time out the two-snapshot classification.
evidence: Plan: 'The canary waits the first snapshots observed holder lease, not a separate wall-clock threshold.'
reconcile-bridge-canary.yml: 'timeout-minutes: 10'
ADR 0031: 'Lease config. DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS = 120; ... C3 wires [reconciler] lock_lease_secs into the acquire call.' — lease is operator-configurable and could exceed the 10-min canary budget
Default 120s is safe; only a misconfigured large lease bites, so this is a minor edge, not a correctness defect for the default path.
findings.finding: The canary waits the holder-observed lease between its two read-only snapshots, but the lease is operator-configurable ([reconciler] lock_lease_secs, blob-sourced) while the canary job runs under a fixed timeout-minutes: 10; the plan never bounds the observed lease against the canary runner timeout, so a large misconfigured lease makes the two-snapshot canary silently time out mid-wait rather than emit a verdict.
findings.location: 'Status snapshot and exact contract' / 'Canary cutover and rollback' — 'The canary waits the first snapshots observed holder lease'
scenarios: An operator raises lock_lease_secs above ~9 minutes; the canary's inter-snapshot sleep exceeds the 10-minute job timeout and the run is killed with no CRASHED/RUNNING verdict, degrading the very crash-detection the story adds.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Require ADR 0094 to explicitly cite ADR 0031's ref-lock fence/lease prior art (the skew-proof lease-expiry rule and single CAS classifier) as the established pattern the last-pass ref and two-witness crash detection extend, rather than presenting the fence witness as new.
evidence: The ADR 0094 content list enumerates 'the authoritative last-pass ref, fixed rich-detail file, write-before-release ordering, separate stalled-fence crash witness, rejected timestamp and accumulating-file alternatives, and rollback' with no explicit cite to ADR 0031.

ADR 0031 (docs/adr/0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md) already documents the fence progress-witness, the skew-proof lease-expiry rule ('the holder is considered dead only if neither the ref oid nor fence advanced over one lease'), DEFAULT_LEASE_SECS=120 carried in the blob, and the single CAS classifier the plan mandates reusing.

Web search confirms this is established prior art: AWS DynamoDB Lock Client docs (lease auto-expiry + heartbeat 'independent of system time'), fencing-token/generation-counter articles, and git-scm's force-with-lease atomic compare-and-swap semantics.

The plan reuses the same primitive ('Reuse the existing CAS and mismatch-classification seams ... do not introduce a second mismatch classifier'), so the crash witness is an extension of a proven in-repo pattern, not a new one.
findings.finding: The ADR 0094 content requirements do not require an explicit cross-reference to the ADR 0031 fence/lease/single-CAS-classifier prior art that the new last-pass ref and two-witness crash witness extend, risking the appearance of a novel invention rather than a documented extension.
findings.location: Plan section 'Architecture record and numbering convention' (ADR 0094 content list); also 'Durable state and writer contract'
scenarios: A future reader of ADR 0094 evaluating whether the two-witness/fence design is novel and whether it duplicates ADR 0031's rationale.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the ADR 0094 content list an explicit 'Relation to ADR 0031' item that states the two-witness crash detection reuses ADR 0031's fence progress-witness, lease-carried-in-blob expiry rule, and single CAS/mismatch classifier, and only adds the last-pass authoritative record on top.
